skills.name: CVE lookup workflow
skills.description: Research a CVE id end to end.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the CVE id; open the NVD page (web.crawl).
2. Extract CVSS, affected versions, CWE.
3. Find patch commits via web.search on the project repo.
4. Summarize: what, where, how bad, fixed-in.
5. Save the brief with file.write.

skills.name: NVD/CPE querying
skills.description: Find CVEs by product and version.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Determine the CPE for the product (web.search).
2. web.search NVD for cpe matches and version ranges.
3. Collect CVE list with severities.
4. Filter by exploitability signals (KEV, PoC existence).
5. Deliver a prioritized table.

skills.name: CWE classification
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Read the finding description carefully.
2. web.search the CWE catalog for candidate classes.
3. Match root cause, not symptom.
4. Note parent/child CWE relationships.
5. Record CWE id with rationale.

skills.name: CVSS v3/v4 scoring
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Parse the vector components from the finding.
2. web.search the FIRST calculator guidance for edge cases.
3. Score and cross-check the vector string.
4. Explain each metric choice in one line.
5. Attach the vector to the report.

skills.name: CISA KEV awareness
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the CVE plus KEV.
2. Note dates and required action.
3. Prioritize KEV-listed items in remediation.
4. Record the KEV entry in notes.
5. Report urgency honestly.

skills.name: Exploit-DB research
skills.description: Find public PoCs for a CVE.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search exploit-db for the CVE/product.
2. Read the PoC source before running anything.
3. Assess quality: works? safe? version-specific?
4. Adapt only for authorized targets.
5. Save the reference in workspace notes.

skills.name: GitHub advisory research
skills.description: Mine GHSA data for a dependency.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search GHSA plus the package name.
2. Check affected version ranges against your lockfile (file.read).
3. Note patched versions.
4. Cross-check with CVE ids.
5. Summarize upgrade needs.

skills.name: PoC triage discipline
skills.description: Evaluate a public exploit before use.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Read the entire PoC (file.read after download).
2. Hunt for malicious side effects (reverse shells, destructive ops).
3. Check target-version applicability.
4. Sandbox it: run only against your lab.
5. Document the verdict.

skills.name: PoC adaptation workflow
skills.description: Adapt a PoC to your environment.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Identify hardcoded values (hosts, offsets, paths) with file.search.
2. Parameterize them with file.patch.
3. Adjust for version differences using the patch diff as a guide.
4. Test in small steps against your lab.
5. Keep an adaptation changelog.

skills.name: Patch diff analysis
skills.description: Turn a patch into an exploit hypothesis.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Obtain the fixed version source (web.search repo).
2. Diff vulnerable vs fixed (process.exec diff or git).
3. Isolate the security-relevant change.
4. Form the exploitation hypothesis from the guard added.
5. Validate against your lab instance.

skills.name: Changelog security mining
skills.description: Extract security notes from release notes.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.crawl the project changelog page.
2. Search for security/CVE mentions with python.run_file.
3. Map releases to fixed issues.
4. Note unpatched older branches.
5. Summarize exposure windows.

skills.name: Disclosure timeline analysis
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Collect dates: report, CVE, patch, PoC release (web.search).
2. Build the timeline.
3. Assess patch-gap exposure.
4. Relate to your asset versions.
5. Report the risk window.

skills.name: Multi-source correlation
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Gather entries for the same issue from each source (web.search).
2. Normalize: id, affected, fixed, severity.
3. Resolve conflicts (prefer vendor for fix versions).
4. Produce a single authoritative record.
5. Save it to the workspace.

skills.name: EPSS context
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the CVE plus EPSS.
2. Note the score and date.
3. Combine with KEV and exposure.
4. Prioritize remediation accordingly.
5. Explain the signal in the report.

skills.name: Vendor advisory parsing
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Open the vendor advisory (web.crawl).
2. Extract affected products/versions exactly.
3. Note workarounds vs full fixes.
4. Check scanner-compatible identifiers.
5. Summarize action items.

skills.name: Mailing list research
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the topic plus oss-security.
2. Read the full thread for exploitability discussion.
3. Note maintainer responses and PoC links.
4. Extract version constraints.
5. Summarize with links.

skills.name: Bug tracker mining
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the project issues for security keywords.
2. Filter resolved-but-unpatched older versions.
3. Note reproducer steps posted publicly.
4. Correlate with your versions.
5. Report exposure.

skills.name: Commit history research
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Browse the repo history around the affected file (web.search links).
2. Locate the introducing commit.
3. Read the surrounding intent.
4. Estimate affected version range.
5. Document with commit ids.

skills.name: Fuzzer findings research
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the project plus OSS-Fuzz issues.
2. Read crash types and stacks.
3. Note which are security-relevant.
4. Check fix status per version.
5. Summarize for your target.

skills.name: Threat actor context
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the CVE plus threat reports.
2. Note observed exploitation patterns.
3. Map to your asset's exposure.
4. Prioritize by real-world targeting.
5. Cite sources in the report.

skills.name: Detection guidance authoring
skills.description: Write detection rules for a vuln class.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Describe the exploit signature from the PoC.
2. Map to log sources available.
3. Draft detection logic (pseudo or SIEM syntax).
4. Propose test events.
5. Save the rule with file.write.

skills.name: Interim mitigation design
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. List available controls (WAF rules, config flags).
2. Assess each against the exploit primitive.
3. Choose minimal-impact mitigations.
4. Document bypass caveats honestly.
5. Provide rollback steps.

skills.name: Weekly intel digest
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search latest KEV and critical advisories.
2. Filter to your stack (file.read inventory).
3. Summarize top 10 with actions.
4. Save the digest with file.write.
5. Present the shortlist in chat.

skills.name: Exploit reuse legality
skills.description: Know the rules for public PoCs.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Check the PoC license before reuse (file.read).
2. Attribute correctly.
3. Respect disclosure norms.
4. Never use PoCs on unauthorized targets.
5. Note constraints in your report.

skills.name: Research note system
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. One file per CVE in the workspace (file.write).
2. Sections: summary, affected, PoC status, notes.
3. Link evidence files.
4. Update after each session.
5. Index all files for search.

skills.name: Local PoC reference library
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Save key PoCs into a workspace folder (file.write).
2. Record source, license, verdict per file.
3. Keep a catalog index.
4. Re-verify after target updates.
5. Clean out stale items.

skills.name: Version fingerprinting
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Gather headers, meta, and banner data (web.headervuln, process.exec curl).
2. Cross-check with behavior probes.
3. Map to CPE for CVE matching.
4. Note uncertainty honestly.
5. Record in the engagement notes.

skills.name: Exploitability triage
skills.description: Decide what is worth deeper work.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Score: exposure, auth requirements, PoC maturity, impact.
2. Rank candidates in a table.
3. Pick the top item; justify.
4. Defer the rest with reasons.
5. Log the decision.

skills.name: Disclosure norms briefing
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the project's security policy.
2. Follow the stated reporting channel.
3. Respect embargo timelines.
4. Never publish unpatched issues.
5. Keep the user informed of obligations.

skills.name: CVE monitoring setup
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Inventory components (file.read manifests).
2. web.search per-component advisory feeds.
3. Summarize a monitoring plan.
4. Save the plan with file.write.
5. Review cadence: weekly.

skills.name: Red team brief template
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Sections: scope, rules, contacts, timeframe.
2. Include explicit out-of-scope items.
3. Define evidence handling.
4. Get sign-off before activity.
5. Store the brief with file.write.

skills.name: Attack surface mapping
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Combine port scan (net.portscan) and crawl (web.crawl).
2. List services, endpoints, and auth modes.
3. Version-fingerprint each (cat_res_version_fingerprinting flow).
4. Prioritize entry points.
5. Save the map with file.write.

skills.name: Initial access planning
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Review the attack surface map.
2. Pick the weakest credible entry point.
3. Define success signals before acting.
4. Prepare rollback/abort criteria.
5. Execute minimally; log everything.

skills.name: Privilege path research
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Inventory privileges gained so far.
2. Enumerate next-hop targets (services, creds, misconfigs).
3. Research known paths via web.search for your stack.
4. Validate hypotheses in the lab.
5. Document the chain.

skills.name: Post-exploitation reporting
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Record actions taken with timestamps.
2. Quantify impact reached (data/systems).
3. Include screenshots/paths as evidence files.
4. Map each action to the rules of engagement.
5. Deliver the full chain report.

skills.name: Purple team loop
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. For each validated finding, draft a detection test.
2. Execute the attack once; verify the alert fires.
3. Tune and re-test.
4. Record results per control.
5. Save the loop log.

skills.name: Vulnerable lab setup
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search deliberately vulnerable apps for the target stack.
2. Set up in an isolated environment only.
3. Document setup steps (file.write).
4. Verify isolation before testing.
5. Keep the lab inventory.

skills.name: Exploit maturity assessment
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Classify: theoretical, functional, reliable, weaponized.
2. Base the grade on evidence from research.
3. Note dependencies (auth, config).
4. Use the grade in prioritization.
5. Cite sources.

skills.name: Zero-day handling ethics
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Confirm the issue is truly unpatched (web.search).
2. Follow coordinated disclosure norms.
3. Limit PoC distribution.
4. Notify the vendor privately.
5. Document your timeline.

skills.name: Bounty program compliance
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Read the program policy fully (web.crawl).
2. Note allowed targets and methods.
3. Respect rate and impact limits.
4. Track findings against the policy.
5. Submit through official channels only.

skills.name: OSINT to asset linking
skills.description: Connect public data to your assets.
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the org plus technology keywords.
2. Note exposed docs, repos, subdomains.
3. Verify each against your scope list.
4. Record provenance.
5. Feed the attack surface map.

skills.name: Research digest writing
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Collect the period's notable findings.
2. Summarize each in 3 lines with links.
3. Rank by relevance to your stack.
4. file.write the digest.
5. Share with the shortlist in chat.

skills.name: Exploit history awareness
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. web.search the CVE plus campaign/malware mentions.
2. Note first-seen dates and actors.
3. Relate to patch adoption.
4. Adjust urgency accordingly.
5. Cite everything.

skills.name: PoC safety testing
skills.instructions:
Workflow:
1. Static review first (file.read).
2. Run inside an isolated VM/container you own.
3. Monitor outbound connections (tcpdump.capture).
4. Never run against production.
5. Record behavior.
